biography_sections.title: Larne freehold applicant and profile attribution
biography_sections.markdown:
James Glasgow of Larne is no.16 among persons applying to register freeholds at the Carrickfergus General Quarter Sessions on 13 January 1831. His December 1830 entry describes houses and land in Upper Glenarm, townland of Larne, with a yearly value of £10.

This is an application published on 24 December 1830, not proof that registration succeeded. Glasgow-3986 is a possible local candidate; another Larne-born adult James who died at Demerara in 1839 remains a competing comparison. It gives no age, occupation, relatives or bridge to the 1795 merchant or 1797 junior. It does not connect Larne to Lisnagaver.

[Belfast News-Letter, 24 December 1830, p.3, County Antrim freehold-registration applications](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574399/)

[Complete newspaper account and held draft](/research/subjects/newspapers-irish-1800-1850/#james-larne-freeholder).

The current live Family section names James-1509; the biography retains the earlier William-1505 attachment. Neither is proved by this newspaper. Existing parentage and possible fatherhood of Alexander-951 remain provisional.

biography_sections.title: The 1821 Larne sibling household: compatible brother only
biography_sections.markdown:
The inspected [Crossle genealogical abstract, page 23, image 00142](https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=S2%2FIRE%2FNAI%2F007634855%2F00142&parentid=IRE%2FNAI%2FGENABS%2F01110626%2F1) records Ann Glasgow, 50, at No. 22 Main Street, Larne, with sister Jane and brother James, both 47, in an account headed 1821 census. The abstract explicitly states the sibling roles for its record subjects. Its reported age for James implies a birth about 1773–1774, compatible with Glasgow-3986’s uncertain circa-1773 birth and Larne setting. It does not identify him as the brother or resolve his adult record sequence.

The independently recorded Ann/Jane household strengthens a possible comparison with the women in the 1832 Newtown lease renewal. [Ann Glasgow-3992](/people/glasgow-3992.html) remains a possible identity for the abstract’s Ann, with a few years’ age difference from her monument, and no same-premises or parent bridge. The monument-defined father [James Glasgow-3991](/people/glasgow-3991.html) died in 1812 and his wife Jane in 1820, so they cannot be the living abstract brother and sister. No existing-profile sibling or parent edge is selected; James-3986’s proposed fatherhood and possible freehold identification retain their earlier grades.

[Catalogue source record](/sources/s-190f0e1ecb50f3ed/) · [Larne and Kilwaughter study](/branches/larne-kilwaughter/#chapter-crossle-larne-siblings-1821). The inspected image is a Crossle abstract, not the original census sheet. Next tests are the 1832 renewal, the precise premises and a named family bridge.

opening: The inspected 1821 Crossle abstract names Ann Glasgow, 50, with sister Jane and brother James, both 47, at No. 22 Main Street, Larne. Glasgow-3986 is compatible with the brother’s age and locality, but that identity is unproved; the Ann/Jane pair strengthens a possible comparison with the 1832 lease renewal. His possible 1830 freehold application and provisional merchant sequence do not establish his parents, siblings or children. The Larne–Lisnagaver link remains unproved.
